Chapter 7. Perspectivism—Seeing Through Many Eyes.
Have you ever noticed that everyone’s looking at the world through their own unique window? The view isn’t quite the same for any two people. What’s totally obvious to one person might be invisible to someone else. That’s really the heart of perspectivism—the idea that there’s no single, absolute truth, but instead, a patchwork of perspectives.
Picture a group of friends sitting around a table, swapping stories about something they all experienced together. One remembers the laughter, another picks up on the tension, and someone else zeroes in on tiny details everyone else missed. Each story is true, in its own way, but none of them capture the whole picture. The truth isn’t just a single point—it’s more like a tapestry, woven from all those different threads.
Most of us don’t even realize how much our own perspective shapes what we see. We just assume our view is the normal one, and forget that others might see things differently. But if you start thinking like a philosopher who really embraces perspectivism, you learn to step outside your own window and try seeing the world through many sets of eyes.
It’s not always comfortable, is it? It means letting go of the idea that your way of seeing things is the only way. It means realizing that every perspective—yours included—has its limits, and that every claim to truth is colored by the person who’s making it.
Imagine a classroom, where the teacher asks each student to describe a painting. One notices the colors, another focuses on the shapes, someone else talks about the feelings it brings up, or maybe even a memory. The teacher smiles, because the real point isn’t to find the right answer—it’s to help everyone appreciate just how rich and varied all these perspectives can be.
Perspectivism isn’t just a recipe for confusion, or a way to say that anything goes. It’s really a call to humility, to curiosity, and to empathy. It’s an invitation to see the world in all its complexity, and to recognize that every single perspective has something valuable to offer.
So, here’s the real challenge—it’s not about defending your own view at all costs, but about learning from others. Let your own perspective be changed, enriched, and deepened by the people around you.
